public_rationale: The January 11, 2021 Switch Transformer report describes a sparse model with 1.6 trillion total parameters [e1]. The Pile announcement of December 31, 2020 describes an 825 GiB training corpus [e2]. Research released on February 24, 2022 documents structural-generalization failures by tested sequence-to-sequence models on COGS [e3]. These sources support large-scale endpoints and contemporary failures, but do not establish billions of dollars in Transformer-directed expenditure, the historical scale starting points or continuity of comparable errors from 1988 through May 14, 2022 [e1] [e2] [e3]. The compound claim remains unresolved because those components are unverified, rather than contradicted, by this evidence [e1] [e2] [e3].
limitations: The technical sources provide no aggregate accounting of Transformer-directed expenditure [e1] [e2] [e3].
The trillion-parameter figure counts total parameters in a sparse model, not parameters active for each input [e1].
The scale endpoints do not establish the claimed megabyte-scale dataset and million-parameter starting points [e1] [e2].
The contemporary COGS findings do not establish continuity from 1988 or show that scaling produced no improvements [e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Billions of dollars have been poured into Transformers, training data sets have grown from megabytes to gigabytes and parameter counts from millions to trillions, yet the discomprehending errors documented in numerous works since 1988 remain.

statement.excerpt: Literally billions of dollars have been poured into Transformers, the underlying technology that drives GPT-3, Gato, and so many others; training data sets have expanded from megabytes to gigabytes, parameter counts from millions to trillions. And yet the discomprehending errors, well-documented in numerous works since 1988, remain.
statement.document_title: The New Science of Alt Intelligence

from_speaker: training data sets have expanded from megabytes to gigabytes
parameter counts from millions to trillions
our_interpretation: This is a compound claim about resources, model scale, and continuing comprehension failures. Supporting the whole claim requires evidence for each material component.
The historical comparison runs from 1988 through publication. The assertion that errors remain concerns systems available by May 14, 2022.

I read dollars as US dollars and poured into Transformers as resources actually devoted to developing this technology. General AI investment, company financing, and expenditure cannot automatically be substituted for one another.
I read discomprehending errors as observable failures of compositional interpretation or generalization, without treating those failures as proof about subjective understanding.
criteria.support_condition: Establish multibillion-dollar resources attributable to Transformer development by publication, the stated growth in training data and parameter counts, and independently documented comparable comprehension failures in early research and contemporary systems.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes that a material component is false, such as a comprehensive Transformer expenditure total below the claimed scale or reliable elimination of the specified failures. Missing expenditure records alone do not contradict the claim.

evidence.explanation: This establishes the trillion-parameter endpoint. These are sparse models' total parameter counts; the paper does not establish expenditure or the complete historical comparison.
This establishes the existence of a large language-model training corpus before publication. It does not identify Marcus's megabyte-scale starting point.

The study compares structure-aware parsers with neural sequence models and finds persistent structural-generalization weaknesses in the latter. This supports the contemporary-failure component, but does not establish continuity from 1988 or the financial component.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Transparent accounting of actual Transformer-directed expenditure through May 14, 2022, separating financing from spending and avoiding double counting; original specifications establishing the claimed dataset and parameter growth; and independent historical and contemporary research documenting comparable failures across the period beginning in 1988.
